summary:
SCOPE. I read every note in public/data/voiced-teachings.json from 7034 to 7476: 443 notes from 34 videos. 235 are opening notes, 190 middlegame and 18 endgame; the student is White in 213 and Black in 230. The `concepts` field is empty on all 443 and `teaches` is filled on 99, so the teaching lives in the prose. I compared the slice with Reader 8's 98-entry catalogue, which covers this same range at a coarser grain (digests/teach.md, Source 8). Spot checks support that catalogue: moveFundamentals 'queen-off-file' (moveFundamentals.ts:65-68, :976) was built from note 7311 in this slice, and forkTrick.ts:126 trickSidestepped does sidestep the trick in 7302-7303. The list below has 59 entries. 46 are acts the coarse read missed or folded into a broader bucket. 13 are acts it already had, re-checked here with details or code facts specific to this slice. Everything is paraphrased. The reference coach's name is never written; the one service file named after him is written as [coach-name]Behaviors.ts.

THE MISSES THAT MATTER MOST (opening and traps first, per F02-F04):
(1) A trap taught with its conditions, plus the final safety check: queens facing each other, kings uncastled, their queen guarded only by its king. Only Review can see this: reviewTeachingPoints.ts:146-166 royalDefenderTarget, called at reviewFullData.ts:849. It also skips pawns (reviewTeachingPoints.ts:152), so 'f7 is guarded only by the king', the most-taught weak point in the opening, is never computed.
(2) A pattern's precondition disappears and the pattern is off. Only the centre-fork trick has this (forkTrick.ts:126). moveInsight.ts:668 greekGift fires only when the engine's best move IS the sacrifice. F04 needs a general tracker.
(3) Deflection without capturing the guard, either by a check or by forcing a recapture somewhere else. No such producer exists. detectRemovalOfGuard needs the guard itself captured (tacticClassifier.ts:457), and tacticsDetector.ts:293-300 suppresses a false skewer in note 7331's own game without adding a deflection read.
(4) Overload where the guard's second job is stopping mate. findOverloadedPieces counts only two attacked pieces worth at least 3 (tacticsDetector.ts:699, :711).
(5) Their move opens a line for your piece, or spends their own blocking resource. theirMoveCost has exactly four kinds (theirMoveCost.ts:23). Its 'hole' kind only fires when a student KNIGHT reaches the square within two jumps (theirMoveCost.ts:35, :82-83), so 'their pawn push gives your bishop c5' (7055-7056) is never said.
(6) A clamp built up over several moves, with the running count. moveIntent's PREVENTS needs the stopped move to be worth at least 100cp (moveIntent.ts:71, :165), so a positional clamp on a freeing push usually stays silent.
(7) Castling denial, in both directions. castleIsOneMoveAway checks attacked transit squares (positionalRead.ts:156-165). castleRoute does not (kingSafety.ts:202-215), yet detectCentralKingDanger (kingSafety.ts:159) and [coach-name]Behaviors.ts:298 build 'get castled' advice on it. That is a latent D10 risk; I read it but did not run it.
(8) Self-interference: a natural move blocks your own piece's line (4 notes). Nothing produces it.
(9) Future scope: judge a piece by the line it will have after your planned pawn moves (3 notes). Nothing produces it.
(10) Your move leaves them one defence, and it is ugly. walkForcedSequence (onlyMoveSequence.ts:57) could walk the forced line but has no production caller (G8.5).

REACH GAPS (S1/F2). Several existing computers reach only one surface:
- speedRunReads runs only on the student's turn (thinkAloud.ts:257).
- autopilotRecapture runs only from PuzzleBoard.tsx:652.
- pieceOptions runs only from chat (coachService.ts:1483).
- sacrificeCompensation runs only in Review (reviewFullData.ts:915, coachFeatureService.ts:2750).
- The opening lecture's 'more testing try' line exists only in Review (reviewOpeningTheory.ts:691-700).
- [coach-name]Behaviors' 'down material' rule runs only in Learn (CoachTeachPage.tsx:293).

Its advice that trading helps the side that is down also contradicts the app's own rule at [coach-name]Behaviors.ts:576-577. The seat guard cannot catch this, because the note's seat does match.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Overload where the guard's second job is stopping mate: both answers lose
teachingMoves.example: A bishop check makes their queen choose. If it takes back, the rook it was guarding falls; if it stays put, it is mate. Name both branches, then the verdict.

teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: PARTIAL. tacticsDetector.ts:690-723 findOverloadedPieces needs two attacked pieces worth at least 3 (:699, :711). A guard whose other duty is a mating square is never found, so the mate-duty case is MISSING.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Deflection without capturing the guard, by a check or by forcing a recapture elsewhere
teachingMoves.example: Their queen is the only guard of the corner rook, so a bishop check drives it off. Later a rook trade forces their queen off e8, and the knight it guarded on e6 is left hanging.
teachingMoves.when: Tactics against a sole defender, middlegame or endgame
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: MISSING. tacticClassifier.ts:457 detectRemovalOfGuard needs the guard itself captured, and tacticsDetector.ts:651 skips king guards. tacticsDetector.ts:293-300 suppresses a false skewer in note 7331's own game (the comment calls it a deflection) but adds no deflection producer. 'deflection' exists only as a puzzle-theme label (tacticClassifierService.ts:23, :47).

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Their move opens a line for your piece and uses up the pawn move that could have closed it
teachingMoves.example: Their early central pawn push opens your bishop's diagonal toward f2. It also spends the pawn that could have stepped to e3 to block that diagonal.

teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: PARTIAL. theirMoveCost.ts:23 has four kinds only (hole, bishop-shut, castling, structure); 'opens a line for your piece' and 'spent a defensive resource' are not among them.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] A new hole taken by a bishop or any other piece, not only a knight
teachingMoves.example: Their pawn steps past c5, so your dark-squared bishop drops straight into that square, with d6 and c6 to follow.
teachingMoves.when: Right after an opponent's pawn advance
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: PARTIAL. theirMoveCost.ts:35 and :82-83 name a new hole only when a student KNIGHT reaches it within two jumps; moveInsight.ts:1102 holeAccess is knight-only too. A hole the bishop takes is never said.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Your move leaves them one defence, and it is an ugly one
teachingMoves.example: A knight jump at f2 looks shallow, but their only way to hold is a knight to the rim. Later, a knight on c7 sets a problem they can only solve with a run of precise moves.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] A clamp on the square they need, built up over several moves, with the running count
teachingMoves.example: The bishop to f4 covers d6, the e5 push squeezes it, and the knight to e4 adds another piece on it. Then say how much control is now on that square.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Level but comfortable: which side is being set the problems

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Proportional response: meet a passive slip with plain development
teachingMoves.example: Their rook-pawn move only lets the pawn be won back and wastes time. There is no need to hunt for a refutation; just develop. Nothing fancy is needed against a harmless sideline, and you play solidly once a pawn up.

teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: MISSING as a framing. The nearest is speedRunReads.ts:68 anyMoveFine.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Size their concession honestly: what it does NOT give you, and what it does
teachingMoves.example: Their capture on d4 doesn't hand you the whole centre, because they can still hit back in the middle, but it frees c3 for your knight for nothing. Your bishop check looks as if it wins the queen, but it doesn't, because a knight can block.

teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: MISSING. theirMoveCost.ts:60 names only positive costs. bluffDetector.ts:37 covers their empty threats, not the student overrating their own move.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Their setup contradicts its own plan
teachingMoves.example: An early f-pawn push belongs with long castling and a pawn storm. Castling short behind it only weakens them a little, so it isn't dangerous.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] The usual square for a piece in this pawn structure
teachingMoves.example: In this ...e5 Sicilian structure the queen's knight goes to d7, almost never c6. The knight's main post later is e5.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Luft made with a pawn that also does a second job
teachingMoves.example: In the ending, air for the king doesn't have to come from the rook pawn. A different pawn push gives the king room, stops a rook raid and prepares to anchor a piece.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Which rook goes to the open file
teachingMoves.example: When converting, put the rook on the open file that doesn't leave its partner buried behind it.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Self-interference: the natural move blocks your own piece's line
teachingMoves.example: Their instinctive bishop move to d2 cuts their own queen off from the d4 pawn. Your knight retreats to e3, not g2, where it would bury the bishop. Your bishop goes to b2, not d2, where a pawn push would deflect it and force your king to move.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] A capture chosen to close lines toward your own king
teachingMoves.example: After the sharp f-pawn thrust, recapturing on e4 with that pawn lowers the risk of your king being opened up.
teachingMoves.when: Opening, with your own king exposed
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: MISSING. kingSafety.ts:56 detectKingExposure reads exposure, but nothing explains a capture as closing a line.

teachingMoves.move: [NEW] Knowledge: a check that also hits a piece can be answered by that piece blocking
teachingMoves.example: Their knight takes on d4 and the queen check looks like a fork, but the knight just drops back to c6 and blocks. So take the knight first, and then the check picks up the bishop.
teachingMoves.when: Tactics around checks
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: PARTIAL. checkMethod.ts:32 teaches the three ways to meet a check, and thinkAloud.ts:145 notYet says 'take the knight first'. Neither names the forked piece blocking as the reason the check fails.

teachingMoves.move: [SEEN, refined] A trap taught with its trigger conditions and the last safety check
teachingMoves.example: Queens face each other, kings are uncastled, and their queen is guarded only by its king. Develop the bishop to c4; if they capture, the check on f7 drags the king away and the queen falls. Before cashing in, confirm no in-between check saves them; here their own pawn blocks it.
teachingMoves.when: An opening trap set by a developing move
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: PARTIAL. reviewTeachingPoints.ts:146-166 royalDefenderTarget is Review-only (reviewFullData.ts:849). There is no live trap computer for the pattern's conditions (F04), and no in-between-check habit in safetyHabits.ts.

teachingMoves.move: [SEEN, refined] The opponent's known slip, punished without fear, and the sacrifice they hope for is bad for them
teachingMoves.example: The early bishop to c5 is a known inaccuracy, so take the centre pawn. The bishop check on f2 that people dread actually loses for them, and retreating the bishop gives up the pawn for nothing.
teachingMoves.when: The opponent leaves book with a popular slip
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: refutedAlternativeCore.ts:159/219, forkTrick.ts:81 and bluffDetector.ts:37.

teachingMoves.move: [SEEN, refined] f7 and f2 as the opening's soft spot
teachingMoves.example: In the opening, link any fast assault with f7, the one weak point within reach. A knight jump toward f2 is the same idea from the other side.
teachingMoves.when: Opening, against passive development
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: PARTIAL. keySquares.ts:97 keyTargetSquares names f7 as a target beside the king. But royalDefenderTarget skips pawns (reviewTeachingPoints.ts:152), so 'only the king guards f7' is never said.

teachingMoves.move: [SEEN, refined] A centralised piece with no support is a target: combine it with another weakness
teachingMoves.example: Their knight in the centre has nothing behind it. Ignore it and hit f7: the pressure there plus the loose knight sets up a double attack.
teachingMoves.when: Opening, after an opponent's pawn grab
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: loosePieces.ts:35 findLoosePieces, moveInsight.ts:83 doubleAttack and latentFork.ts:161.

teachingMoves.move: [SEEN] Several wrong ways first, each with its refutation, then the clean move
teachingMoves.example: Against the pin, pushing the f-pawn weakens your king, and the counter-pin with the bishop gets kicked so the e4 pawn drops. So simply develop to d3.
teachingMoves.when: Decision points in the opening
teachingMoves.frequency: 2 long notes (7218-7219); about 22 notes reject a tempting or popular move
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: refutedAlternativeCore.ts:159 candidatesFromAmateur (what players at the student's level play) and deliberation.ts:144 (engine candidates).

teachingMoves.move: [SEEN, this slice] The opening's ideas, given as a list
teachingMoves.example: This defence has two ideas: a solid claim on d5 backed by e6, and quick kingside development without passive pieces.
teachingMoves.when: First moves of a named opening
teachingMoves.frequency: 3 notes (7042-7044); opening names or theory status appear in about 71 notes
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: PARTIAL. openingIdentity.ts:85 openingIdentityLine covers what the opening provokes, gambits, aims and sharpness, but not a list of its ideas.

teachingMoves.move: [SEEN] What a gambit's material bought, and how to defuse it
teachingMoves.example: The pawn bought a lead in development. Against an unfamiliar gambit, develop, leave their advanced knight alone, and remember you can give the pawn back to reach an ending.
teachingMoves.when: Gambits
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: PARTIAL. openingIdentity.ts:85 states the gambit fact, and sacrificeCompensation (reviewSacrifice.ts:44) is Review-only.

teachingMoves.move: [SEEN] One move, several jobs
teachingMoves.example: The queen steps to e1 instead of pushing e5 at once: it avoids the queen trade and heads for an attacking post.
teachingMoves.when: Quiet moves with more than one purpose
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: moveIntent.ts:124 (prevents plus prepares). moveFundamentals.ts:65-68/:976 'queen-off-file' was written from note 7311 in this slice.

teachingMoves.move: [SEEN] Kick a piece with a pawn and gain time
teachingMoves.example: Push the pawn at the annoying knight so it has to go back.
teachingMoves.when: The opponent has an advanced piece
teachingMoves.computerThatCouldProduceIt: moveFundamentals.ts:369-391 'tempo'.

teachingMoves.move: [SEEN] Call back to the earlier preparation
teachingMoves.example: Good thing the bishop went back to b3 earlier. The whole point of the earlier pawn move was to make sure the rook could lift.
